_comment_method_overrides: rejection_abc thresholds at tol_init and stops at k accepted, while the
asynchronous scheduler treats tol_init as a STARTING bandwidth and tightens
from there. At the shared value this arm accepted 85.9% of prior draws and
stopped after ~100 evaluations, so its reported posterior was the prior.
The override is the tolerance at which the budget yields k accepted: 0.2% of prior draws (k=100 of the 50,000 budget).
_comment_rejection: rejection_abc reports the k closest of everything it evaluates
(rejection_mode defaults to best_k), so it needs no tolerance constant and
reports at the k-th order statistic of its own draws -- the same rule the
asynchronous arm uses. Before 2026-09-19 it thresholded at the shared
tol_init, which the asynchronous scheduler needs LOOSE because it treats it
as a starting bandwidth; at that value this arm accepted most of the prior
and stopped after ~100 evaluations, reporting a prior sample.

_comment: Matched-EVALUATION-COUNT g-and-k run, which the paper names as the control
it has not run (sec:limitations vii). max_wall_time_s is removed so the
generation budget binds: propulate_budget_mode=total_simulations then gives
exactly max_simulations evaluations across ranks, instead of the wall clock
deciding how many each arm gets.
Purpose: the async arm's k-th order statistic at 50,000 evaluations was
measured at 0.062 on a tol_init=10.0 history. The bandwidth transient is
~7.3 halvings from 10.0 and costs of order 1,200 evaluations each, so up to
a fifth of a 50,000 prefix may be spent walking the bandwidth down. If that
degrades SAMPLING and not merely reporting, 0.062 is pessimistic.
